newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel pulls off lows, Norilsk news absorbed.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel pulls off lows, Norilsk news absorbed.

text.p: Nickel whipped back from softer levels during LME ring trading on Tuesday morning even after news that workers decided not to halt output at Russia's huge Norislk complex.
Three month prices bounced from a low of $7,675 despite a statement by Norilsk Nickel that its unions had agreed to drop all plans to disrupt output through June 30.
Prices surged in the last minutes of the official ring in large volumes thought to be fund-based, regaining the $7,800 level.
"Maybe they had been expecting the news so they turned around on the fact," one floor trader said.
During the kerb, prices drifted down to finish the morning at $7,760, down $60 from Monday's afternoon kerb.
The lows had been touched after LME inventories increased by 846 tonnnes as fund selling re-emerged on the pre-market.
The market had seen a good run up to $8,325 earlier in the month but chartists noted that the 10-day moving average looked like it was about to make a bearish cross below the 30-day average.
"I'd be a buyer around $7,700, but if it closes below $7,650, it would look bad," another floor trader said before prices bounced.
A fall in aluminium stocks of 8,775 tonnnes was not enough to restrain broad-based selling, which pressured prices below the $1,650 level.
The market may even test its recent low of $1,637 before consolidating and trying to re-challenge the $1,701 high achieved on March 4, a floor trader said.
Copper held to a narrow trading band after stocks declined by 4,300 tonnes, finishing the morning only $5 weaker at $2,362.
Prices were well within the recent range of $2,305-$2,390 and good support was pegged around $2,350, where the 10-day and 30-day moving averages were converging.
The premium of cash over three months was barely easier at $53/$58 and the main lump of tightness, the May/June spread came in to be bid at a $42 backwardation from $47 on Monday morning.
Zinc, which saw a 1,350 draw in stocks, came off its low of $1,284 and finished the kerb only $4 weaker at $1,290.
Speculators had targeted the market earlier in the morning but the major uptrend was still intact and prices were seen consolidating ahead of another stab at breaking above the recent $1,307 peak.
Lead saw some Chinese selling and prices edged lower to $674, but volume was thin and by the end of the kerb prices had come back to be indicated at $678/79 versus $679 on Friday afternoon.
Tin lost $50 to $5,820 and some analysts are targeting a slump to $5,780 before the market regains its poise.
Alloy lost ground along with the primary market ending the morning at $1,535/40 versus $1,545/55.
